title: IBM Watson wins Jeopardy
one_line: A question-answering machine beats two human champions and becomes the face of AI in medicine before it ever touched a patient.

title: IBM launches Watson Health
one_line: IBM stands up a health unit and buys its way in for about $4bn [reported], promising Watson would read oncology like a specialist.

title: DeepMind Streams goes live at the Royal Free
one_line: An AI-branded kidney-injury alert app ships to a London hospital on a data-sharing deal covering about 1.6m patient records [reported].

title: UK regulator rules the Streams data deal broke the law
one_line: The privacy regulator finds the hospital handed over patient data unlawfully; no fine, but the first shot across the bow on health-data consent [reported].

title: FDA clears IDx-DR, the first autonomous diagnostic AI
one_line: De Novo authorization for a tool that reads eyes for diabetic retinopathy with no doctor in the loop, the first AI allowed to diagnose on its own [disclosed].

title: AlphaFold wins CASP13
one_line: DeepMind's first protein-folding model tops the field's benchmark contest, a strong result that still leaves the problem unsolved.

title: Nuance ships Dragon Ambient eXperience (DAX)
one_line: The ambient-scribe idea, an AI that listens to the visit and writes the note, goes commercial and defines the category doctors would actually adopt [reported].

title: Viz.ai wins the first AI add-on payment from Medicare
one_line: CMS grants a stroke-triage tool a temporary New Technology Add-on Payment of up to $1,040 per use, the first time a US public payer pays extra for AI [disclosed].

title: AlphaFold2 solves protein folding at CASP14
one_line: The second model scores about 92 on a 100-point accuracy test [disclosed], and the contest organizers call a 50-year grand-challenge effectively solved.

title: FDA publishes its AI/ML Action Plan
one_line: The regulator lays out how it will oversee learning software and floats letting devices update under a pre-agreed plan instead of re-filing each change [disclosed].

title: The AlphaFold protein-structure database opens
one_line: DeepMind and a public genomics lab release structures for a first tranche of proteins for free [disclosed], later scaling past 200m and turning a moat into a commons.

title: AMA creates an AI taxonomy for billing codes
one_line: The body that writes US procedure codes adds a framework sorting AI into assistive, augmentative, and autonomous, the plumbing before anything gets paid [disclosed].

title: Isomorphic Labs is founded
one_line: Alphabet spins AlphaFold's drug ambitions into a standalone company, betting the protein breakthrough can be turned into medicines.

title: IBM sells Watson Health for parts
one_line: The oncology-AI flagship that cost about $4bn to build is sold to a private-equity firm for about $1.07bn [reported] and renamed, closing the Watson-in-medicine story.

title: ChatGPT is released
one_line: A general-purpose chatbot goes public and, within weeks, clinicians start using it to draft notes and answer questions it was never approved for.

title: ChatGPT is shown to nearly pass the US medical licensing exam
one_line: A published study puts the model at or near the ~60% passing line across all three exam steps [disclosed], the moment clinical use stopped being hypothetical.

title: Babylon Health files for bankruptcy
one_line: The AI-symptom-checker unicorn, worth about $2bn at its 2021 SPAC listing [reported], liquidates, the clearest sign that an AI demo is not a business.

title: Isomorphic signs Lilly and Novartis for up to ~$3bn
one_line: Two pharma deals with about $83m paid upfront against roughly $2.9bn in milestones [disclosed], the template for how AI-drug deals are really structured: cheap staged bets.

title: FFR-CT graduates to a permanent national billing code
one_line: A heart-blood-flow AI collapses four temporary codes into one permanent Category I code effective this year [disclosed], the rare AI tool with a durable payment path.

title: AlphaFold3 is released
one_line: The third model extends beyond proteins to how they bind DNA, drugs, and other molecules, moving closer to the chemistry that matters for medicines.

title: Tempus AI goes public
one_line: The multi-data diagnostics-and-data platform lists on Nasdaq at $37 a share, raising about $410m [disclosed], the first big pure-play healthcare-AI IPO.

title: AlphaFold's creators win the Nobel Prize in Chemistry
one_line: DeepMind's Hassabis and Jumper share the prize [disclosed], the field's scientific high-water mark, and a reminder the science ran years ahead of the business.

title: Recursion completes its merger with Exscientia
one_line: Two of the loudest AI-drug names combine in an all-stock deal valuing Exscientia at about $650m [reported], consolidation driven by thin pipelines, not strength.

title: The Health Tech Investment Act is introduced
one_line: A Senate bill (S.1399) would create a defined Medicare payment category for algorithm-based services with at least five years of separate pay [disclosed]; that it is needed at all is the tell there is no durable AI payment path today.

title: Caris Life Sciences goes public
one_line: The precision-oncology lab raises about $494m on Nasdaq and pops on day one [disclosed], the second major diagnostics-data IPO in a year.

title: Epic ships its own ambient AI scribe into the chart
one_line: The dominant records system builds note-writing straight into the workflow at a rumored ~$80 per provider per month [sell-side], and the landlord becomes the competitor to the scribe startups renting its rails.
